title: Keepsite build questionnaire
lead: This is the long one, and the only homework in the process. Your answers save as you go, so you can stop and come back.

questions.label: In a sentence or two, what does your business do?
What are the main services, products, or offers you want represented on your website?
Which of those would you most like to grow?
Are there any services you offer but don't particularly want to promote or grow?
Where do you work or serve customers?
questions.help: For example: Spanish Fork, Utah County, statewide, nationwide, online, travel-based.

questions.label: Are there specific towns, regions, or areas where you'd especially like more business?
Tell us a little about the customers you love working with. What are they usually looking for when they come to you?
What tends to matter most to them when choosing a business like yours?
questions.help: For example: trust, experience, style, price, convenience, personality, speed, quality, customization, location, expertise.

questions.label: What questions do potential customers ask you over and over?
questions.help: Think about DMs, emails, calls, consultations, comments, or conversations in person. Even 3–5 questions is incredibly helpful.

questions.label: What do you wish potential customers understood before contacting you?
Why do you think your best customers choose you?
What is the #1 thing you want someone to do after visiting your website?
Is there a second action you'd like visitors to take?
When someone lands on your website for the first time, what are the most important things you want them to understand about your business?
Which pages or areas do you know you want?
Are there any services, locations, audiences, or specialties you think may deserve their own page?
questions.help: A rough guess is fine. We'll also make recommendations based on what people are searching for and how the site should be organized.

sections.help: Think about the homepage direction you already selected. Now tell us what information feels most important to include as someone scrolls.

questions.label: Which sections would you like your homepage to include?

sections.legend: What does your website need to do?
sections.help: Think less about how the site looks and more about what would make it useful for you and your customers.

questions.label: Which features would be helpful for your business?
Are you already using any tools we should connect to the website?
questions.help: Examples: HoneyBook, Dubsado, Calendly, Acuity, Square, Shopify, Stripe, Mailchimp, Flodesk, ConvertKit, Google Calendar, Eventbrite, another booking, CRM, email, or payment tool. Please include links if helpful.

sections.help: We already have your overall homepage direction, so this isn't about choosing another design. We're looking for specific ideas you like.

questions.label: Are there any websites with a feature, page, section, or interaction you love?
questions.help: Paste the link and tell us what you like about it. For example: 'I love how their services are organized.' 'I like how their gallery works.' 'Their booking process feels really easy.'

sections.help: You do not need to write your website copy yet. For now, we want to know where the best raw material already lives.

questions.label: Where can we learn the most about your business?
questions.help: Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, Google Business Profile, existing brochures, pricing guides, PDFs, email templates, client guides, proposals, FAQs, a previous website. Please share links where possible.

questions.label: Are there specific Instagram posts, Reels, captions, or other pieces of content that feel especially "you"?
Are there posts or topics that consistently get a strong response from your audience?
Are there things you find yourself explaining to customers again and again?
Are there topics you could talk about all day?
questions.help: These may become website resources, FAQs, or future blog topics.

sections.help: You do not need to know anything about SEO for this section. We're looking for what you already know about your customers.

questions.label: If someone who had never heard of you needed exactly what you offer, what do you think they might type into Google?
questions.help: Take a guess. There are no wrong answers.

questions.label: What words do your customers use to describe what you do?
Are there words you use in your industry that your customers probably wouldn't?
Who do you consider similar businesses or competitors?
questions.help: They do not have to be direct competitors. Try to list at least 3 with a link to their socials, Google profile, or website.

questions.label: Are there particular services, locations, questions, or topics you'd love to be easier to find online for?
Is there anything about your personality or business that you feel your current online presence does not show well enough?

sections.legend: Why people feel good hiring you

questions.label: What helps someone feel confident choosing you?
Where can we find your existing reviews or testimonials?
Do you have any awards, certifications, press mentions, partnerships, or credentials we should know about?
Are there certain times of year that are especially important for your business?
Are there services you want to promote at particular times of year?
Do you have any launches, events, busy seasons, booking windows, or important dates coming up?
If your new website does one thing really well, what do you hope it is?
Is there anything else you want us to know before we start building?
questions.help: You do not need to have everything figured out. Give us what you know now, and we'll keep learning as we build.
